applies_why: The judge text does the thing the rule governs by making Isaiah 7:14's virgin/young-woman wording and prophetic application two senses and then declaring the issue UNDERDETERMINED.
quote: D5 vs C5 (Isaiah 7:14): UNDERDETERMINED -- Challenger answered the virgin and young-woman wording in [DR3] and defender answered the prophetic application in [CR2] and [CR3].
rule_words: That a single verse does not state a link or its contrary is never a ground for STANDS or UNDERDETERMINED, for either side. A verse that carries two senses at once is not open. Both senses stand.
room: "A verse that carries two senses at once is not open. Both senses stand" — I weighed (1) treating the virgin/young-woman wording and the prophetic application as two senses that make the verse open/underdetermined, against (2) the rule's requirement that both senses stand so the verse is not open on that basis.
why: K-S2 says a verse carrying two senses is not open and both senses stand, so an UNDERDETERMINED verdict resting on those two senses breaches the rule.
